title: Home Protection Plans: Moving the Plan Fee Between Bills
content:
A Home Protection Plan fee is carried either on the bill of a Beacon Ridge electricity or gas agreement or on a direct invoice. These terms govern when and where the fee moves.

## Terms

1. **Closed agreement.** When the Beacon Ridge electricity or gas agreement named to carry the plan fee closes, the plan is not cancelled. Its fee moves to another active Beacon Ridge residential energy agreement at the same premise when one exists, and otherwise to direct invoice.
2. **Customer request.** A customer may also ask to move billing between those methods at any time, subject to the same requirements as at enrollment.
3. **No effect on cover.** Coverage, the waiting period and the plan year are unaffected by a billing change.

## Where the fee goes when the named agreement closes

| Another active Beacon Ridge residential energy agreement at the same premise | Fee moves to |
|---|---|
| Exists | That agreement's bill |
| Does not exist | Direct invoice |

## Illustrations (hypothetical holdings)

1. The plan fee rides on the premise's Beacon Ridge electricity agreement, which closes. The premise also has an active Beacon Ridge residential gas agreement. The plan stays in force and its fee moves to the gas agreement's bill.
2. The plan fee rides on the premise's Beacon Ridge gas agreement, which closes, and no other Beacon Ridge energy agreement at that premise is active. The plan stays in force and its fee moves to direct invoice.
3. In either case the plan's status, coverage start date and plan year are the same after the change as before it.
